 Gold Rate Today, November 12: Gold Becomes Slightly Cheaper In India As 24K Rate Drops To Rs 14,197 Per Gram, Silver At Rs 1,99,900 Per Kg; Check City-Wise Prices 
 Gold prices in India on November 12, 2026, stand at ₹14,197 per gram for 24K gold and ₹13,014 for 22K gold. Silver is priced at ₹199.90 per gram. Check the latest gold and silver rates, city-wise prices and factors buyers should consider before purchasing. 
 By: Zainab Khanam 
Last Updated: November 12, 2026 07:45:32 IST
 Gold Rate Today, November 12, 2026: Check 24K, 22K and 18K Gold Prices in India | Photo: AI-Generated 
 0 
 Gold prices in India remained slightly lower on Thursday, November 12, with 24-karat gold priced at ₹14,197 per gram. The rate for 22-karat gold stood at ₹13,014 per gram, while 18-karat gold was available at ₹10,648 per gram, according to indicative market rates.
 Silver prices also recorded a marginal decline. The metal was priced at ₹199.90 per gram, or ₹1,99,900 per kilogram. Gold and silver prices can vary across cities depending on local market conditions, jeweller pricing and applicable charges. Buyers should confirm the latest rates with their jewellery store before making a purchase.

 The silver rate is the same across the major cities listed in the supplied price data, including Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai, Kolkata, Bengaluru, Hyderabad and Pune. 
 What influences gold prices in India? 
 Gold prices in India are shaped by several domestic and international factors. 
 International bullion prices: Changes in global gold prices influence rates in the Indian market. 
 Rupee-dollar exchange rate: A weaker rupee can make imported gold more expensive. 
 Interest rates: Changes in interest-rate expectations can affect investment demand for gold. 
 Geopolitical developments: Global conflicts and economic uncertainty can increase demand for gold as a safe-haven asset. 
 Import duties and taxes: Government levies contribute to the domestic cost of gold. 
 Jewellery demand: Buying activity during festivals and wedding seasons can influence local prices. 
 Silver prices are also affected by international market movements, currency fluctuations and industrial demand. 
 What should buyers check before purchasing gold and silver? 
 Customers should verify the purity of gold jewellery and look for the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) hallmark before buying. Checking the net gold weight, making charges and any wastage charges is equally important. 
 The final jewellery bill generally includes 3% GST, in addition to applicable making charges. This means the amount paid at the store can be higher than the displayed price of gold. 
 Silver buyers should also check the metal’s purity, weight and additional charges before completing a purchase. Comparing the final bills offered by different jewellers can help customers make a more informed decision. 
 The gold and silver rates mentioned above are indicative and do not include all applicable taxes and levies. Buyers should confirm the final price with their local jeweller before making a transaction.
